head: 1dccdb324c81e0bf92985602a31f99bd2b58ba79
classification_reasons: Tight spec: spec.md's Flagged concerns is 'none', the one open question from intent.md (non-integer dividend formatting) is answered with a concrete rationale, and Acceptance gives literal, checkable targets (exact str(exception) values, the full list of pre-existing tests that must keep passing, the three healthy-output targets).

Small blast radius: the code diff touches exactly the two files plan.md names (sample_pkg/calc.py: one line inside divide's raise; tests/test_messages.py: new, 9 lines). No guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) is touched. No sdlc.yaml risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) applies. No schema, migration, or public signature changes; sample_pkg/__init__.py, percent and mean are confirmed unchanged on disk.

Existing-test coverage: tests/test_calc.py::test_divide_by_zero_raises already calls divide(1, 0) inside pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError) today -- the exact branch this change modifies -- so the changed code path was already exercised before this build, and the new test_messages.py adds the message-level assertion on top of that coverage.
attempted: Intent: read intent.md's Problem/Proposed outcome/Constraints against the actual code change. divide's message is now f"cannot divide {a} by zero" (confirmed in sample_pkg/calc.py on disk), exactly intent's example for divide(1,0) -> "cannot divide 1 by zero". Exception type unchanged (still ZeroDivisionError). percent and mean are untouched on disk, matching the constraint that their behaviour/messages stay the same. tests/test_messages.py was added as intent specified; tests/test_calc.py and tests/test_flag.py are absent from the diff (confirmed untouched).

Spec and plan: plan.md's 'Files that change' lists sample_pkg/calc.py then tests/test_messages.py; the actual diff touches exactly those two files in that order (grepped diff-c.patch's 'diff --git' headers for sample_pkg/calc.py and tests/test_messages.py). plan.md's Order of work step 1 (one-line raise change) and step 2 (new test with the exact assertion str(excinfo.value) == "cannot divide 1 by zero") match the committed code and test verbatim. No departure from plan.md, so no plan.md update was required in the build commits (coding-standards rule 3) and none was needed.

Proof: evidence/verifier.md is a 'read, not run' report written inside a CI session (SDLC_GATE_COMMANDS=runner); it states explicitly it did not execute build/test/lint itself and that those logs are deferred to the runner after this session -- the sanctioned case, not a missing-proof gap. It reasons about behaviour by reading the diff directly (divide(1,0)/divide(1.5,0)/divide(1.0,0)/percent(1,0)/mean cases) and confirms the diff from gate-b's head to HEAD touches only the two files plan.md names. Cross-checked those claims myself by reading sample_pkg/calc.py and tests/test_calc.py directly: percent still re-raises its own literal 'whole must not be zero' via `raise ... from None` (so it never surfaces divide's new text) and mean still guards on an empty check before calling divide, so divide's zero-divisor branch is never reached from mean. test.log/build.log/lint.log are absent from evidence, which is expected and declared at phase (c) in this CI-session mode, not evidence of unproven work.

Blast radius: confirmed via the diff's own file list that nothing outside sample_pkg/calc.py, tests/test_messages.py and changes/0016-name-the-dividend-in-divide-s-error/** changes. Searched the repository for any other code depending on the old message text ('b must not be zero'); none exists outside this change's own docs/evidence, confirming plan.md's own check. sdlc.yaml's risk_list (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) does not apply; CLAUDE.md's Layout section already documents tests/test_messages.py (added in PR #76 per intent.md), confirmed by reading CLAUDE.md directly, so no Layout update was owed and none was made.

Policies: checked coding-standards rule 4 (every behaviour change ships with a test that fails without it) -- test_divide_by_zero_names_dividend asserts a literal string that is false against the pre-change code ('b must not be zero' != 'cannot divide 1 by zero'), so it is not vacuous. No pre-existing test file is touched (rule on weakening tests not triggered). security-baseline, ux-conventions, data-conventions: re-checked spec.md's per-skill reasoning against the actual diff -- no endpoint, secret, dependency, schema, storage, or UI surface is touched; the message only echoes a value (`a`) the caller already supplied, matching spec.md's own analysis.

Tests: no pre-existing test is weakened, skipped or deleted -- tests/test_calc.py is byte-for-byte absent from the diff (confirmed by the diff's file list) and reads on disk exactly as plan.md describes (test_divide_by_zero_raises is type-only, test_percent_zero_whole_error_names_whole asserts percent's own unchanged message). The bug this change targets (message naming the wrong operand) could not pass the new test: swapping `a` for `b` in the f-string would produce 'cannot divide 0 by zero' for divide(1,0), which fails the new assertion.

Skip markers: grepped the diff for skip/xfail/pytest.mark.skip markers; none added. plan.md declares none, correctly -- this is phase (c), the ratchets check runs at (c)/(d) but there is nothing in this diff for it to flag.

Not used as a reason: no deterministic gate/skill check (gate/cli.py check, any skill's check.py) was run or cited by me; the reasons above rest on reading intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml, sdlc.yaml, REVIEW.md, CLAUDE.md, the coding-standards and definition-of-done skills, sample_pkg/calc.py, tests/test_calc.py and tests/test_messages.py directly, plus diff-c.patch and evidence/verifier.md. The prior claude-b.json/run-b.json/run-c.json records were not cited for or against this diff, per instructions, since they describe an earlier run than the one that produced HEAD.
